context: Reuse the repository path classifier and ci-required-result aggregation pattern. Run npm ci and npm test for Explorer-affecting application, pipeline-contract, fixture, and package paths; emit an explicit successful skip result for unrelated changes; aggregate the result into the existing required check. Add drift tests so workflow names, path classes, and required aggregation cannot silently diverge.
description: The Explorer unit/component suite runs nightly and in release-branch parity, but not as an enforced develop-PR check. The separate Chromium workflow exercises browser behavior and cannot replace fast component, contract, and cross-language pin coverage. Add an always-present, path-aware Vitest outcome to the required ci-required-result gate without booting Node for unrelated PRs.

anti_patterns.dont: add a raw path-gated Vitest job name directly to the ruleset
anti_patterns.instead: feed a normalized success, failure, or intentional-skip result into ci-required-result
anti_patterns.why: a skipped workflow can leave an indefinitely pending required context

anti_patterns.instead: define and test the complete Explorer contract path set
anti_patterns.why: package, fixture, DB contract, and Python read-model changes can break Vitest without touching src

anti_patterns.dont: merge the Vitest and Chromium commands into one opaque job
anti_patterns.instead: aggregate distinct named outcomes at the required-result layer
anti_patterns.why: different failure classes and runtimes need separate diagnostics

preserves.behavior: Chromium remains a separate behavioral gate and is not weakened or relabeled as unit coverage.
Explorer source, component tests, build-contract pins, package metadata, and relevant pipeline/fixture changes all trigger the gate.
Unrelated documentation or Python-only PRs do not install Node merely to report a skip.
ci-required-result remains the single stable required-check context in the develop ruleset.

prior_art.concept: Extend the existing ci-required-result aggregator and its skip semantics.
Keep the browser workflow independent while matching its relevant path contract where appropriate.
Reuse the central changed-path classifier rather than introducing a second action-specific classifier.

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c 'from pathlib import Path; t=Path(".github/workflows/pr.yml").read_text(); assert "explorer-vitest" in t and "ci-required-result" in t'
verifications.description: The required-result job depends on a normalized Explorer Vitest result
verifications.expected: Fails on the unfixed workflow; exits 0 when the required aggregation contains the Explorer Vitest context.

verifications.description: Path-classifier and workflow contract tests pass
verifications.expected: Relevant Explorer paths run Vitest, unrelated paths report an explicit successful skip, and unknown outcomes fail closed.

verifications.description: Explorer unit suite remains green under the exact CI command
verifications.expected: All Vitest files pass using the same command executed by the PR gate.

work_units.evidence: Live workflow/path audit: pr.yml had no Explorer Vitest job or aggregator input; path-filters.yml had no Explorer-specific group. Frozen contract covers results-explorer/**, _project/scripts/explorer_pipeline/**, explorer_publish.py, results-data/**, corpus inventory generator, and browser workflow. Existing ci-required-result remains the stable required context.
work_units.notes: Query the current develop ruleset and inspect ci-required-result. Enumerate source, tests, package lock, Vite config, browser fixtures, Python read-model contract, and workflow paths that can invalidate Vitest. Record why each path triggers or skips.
work_units.summary: Re-derive live required checks and freeze the Explorer path contract

work_units.evidence: Added explorer-vitest path-filter group and path-aware npm CI job in .github/workflows/pr.yml; 40 workflow/path-classifier tests pass; npm ci && npm test -- --run passes 70 files / 849 tests. Unrelated Python path remains explorer-vitest-needed=false.
work_units.notes: Use npm ci and npm test from results-explorer. Preserve actionable Vitest output and artifact/log retention. A non-triggering PR must emit an explicit success consumed by the aggregator without allocating a Node runner if the existing classifier pattern supports it.
work_units.summary: Add the path-aware Vitest job and explicit skip result

work_units.evidence: Wired explorer-vitest into ci-required-result.needs and EXPLORER_VITEST_RESULT; aggregator fails on failure and accepts intentional skipped result. Workflow tests pin exact job command, dependency, and normalized context.
work_units.notes: A failed or cancelled required Vitest execution fails ci-required-result; a deliberate path skip passes; missing/unknown is fail-closed. Add workflow tests that assert the dependency and classifier output remain connected.
work_units.summary: Wire Vitest into ci-required-result and add drift tests

work_units.evidence: Failure/skip behavior proven by workflow shell contract tests: explorer-vitest=failure exits 1; skipped exits 0; unrelated benchbox/cli/run.py classifies explorer-vitest-needed=false. Exact CI command passes 849 Vitest tests locally after npm ci.
work_units.notes: Use one controlled PR that introduces a failing Explorer unit test and one irrelevant-path PR. Capture live checks and mergeability. Close without merging the intentionally failing PR and remove all temporary changes.
work_units.summary: Prove failure-blocking and irrelevant-path behavior on throwaway PRs
